description: Design a number container system. Support change(index, number) to set the number at index, and find(number) to return the smallest index with that number (or -1 if not found).
intuition: Maintain two mappings: index-to-number and number-to-sorted-indices. On change, remove the index from the old number's set and add it to the new number's set. Finding the smallest index is just accessing the front of the sorted set.
approach: Use a dict mapping index -> number and a dict mapping number -> sorted set of indices. Use a SortedList or heap with lazy deletion.
jsWalkthrough:
Operations: find(10), change(2,10), change(1,10), change(3,10), change(5,10), find(10), change(1,20), find(10)
find(10): numToIdx has no 10 -> return -1
change(2,10): idxToNum[2]=10, heap[10]=[2]
change(1,10): idxToNum[1]=10, heap[10]=[1,2]
change(3,10): idxToNum[3]=10, heap[10]=[1,2,3]
change(5,10): idxToNum[5]=10, heap[10]=[1,2,3,5]
find(10): front=1, idxToNum[1]=10 -> return 1
change(1,20): idxToNum[1]=20, heap[20]=[1]
find(10): front=1, idxToNum[1]=20 (stale, discard). front=2, idxToNum[2]=10 -> return 2
explanation:
1. idx_to_num maps each index to its current number.
2. num_to_idx maps each number to a sorted set of indices.
3. On change: remove index from old number's set, add to new number's set.
4. On find: return the smallest index in the number's sorted set.
5. SortedList provides O(log n) add, remove, and min access.
hints: Maintain a mapping from number to sorted set of indices.
On change, remove the old mapping and add the new one.
The smallest index is always at the front of the sorted set.
